input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The OR composition checks for retry_all when deciding whether to flatten an existing retry_any.
- failure path: with `(A & B) | C`, the retry_all on the left is spliced into the retry_any as if it were a plain list of predicates, so the combination behaves as `A | B | C`: a retry fires when only A holds although the author required A and B together; no error is raised and the extra retries are silent

Reviewer finding
- description: The async `__ror__` flattens using `isinstance(other, retry_all)`, but it is defined on the async `retry_any`, so the check should be against `retry_any`. The base-class version in tenacity/retry.py correctly checks `retry_any`. Here `retry_all.retries` are merged into a `retry_any`.
- rationale: Trigger: `retry_all(a, b) | async_retry_any(c)`. The code runs `retry_any(a, b, c)`, so the AND-group is flattened into an OR. A retry that should fire only when both a and b hold now fires when a alone holds. This silently changes retry behavior. `retry_all` here is the async class (the name resolves at call time), and `retry_any` and `retry_all` are separate classes.
critique: The finding describes the same fault as the label. The OR composition (`__ror__`) uses the wrong isinstance check against `retry_all` instead of `retry_any`, so an AND-group is spliced into the OR as `A | B | C` and retries silently fire when only A holds. The mechanism and consequence are identical.
